text.p: Leading Swedish bank Handelsbanken , which earlier said it bought Estonian broker Aktoris, on Monday said it was looking beyond Estonia and wanted to get involved in Latvian and Lithuanian markets.
"We have a long-term commitment to the Baltic countries," Handelsbanken Tallinn representative office head Bo Kragh told a news conference.
"Naturally our long-term perspective includes activities in your neighbouring countres of Latvia and Lithuania. But we have decided to start here," Kragh said.
But Handelsbanken has not yet made any formal decisions on pan-Baltic expansion and is still at the research stage.
"We have some thinking to do in regards to these (Latvian and Lithuanian) markets," Kragh added.
Estonia is seen as the most advanced of the Baltic financial markets with many companies planning to list their shares on the stock exchange.
However, both local and foreign interest to the Latvian and Lithuanian markets have been increasing.
"There is no decision as yet. It depends on the market, but the aim is as quickly as possible," Aktoris managing director Auli Kumpulainen said of expansion into the other markets.
